name: Hungaroring

sources.geometry: OpenStreetMap highway=raceway ways "Hungaroring" (Overpass API, (c) OSM contributors, ODbL). Start/finish line placed at the line just ahead of the grid boxes on aerial imagery (Esri World Imagery, used only to locate the line).
sources.width: Published: FIA CEZ circuit facts give 11-15 m; OSM width=15 on the main straight. Mapped: main straight to Turn 1 15 m, Turn 12 13 m, Turn 6-7 chicane 11 m, elsewhere 12.5 m.
sources.elevation: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM (Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N47_00_E019_00_DEM, https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com), robust median + ~250 m smoothing.
sources.camber: none (30 m surface model cannot resolve crossfall).
sources.pit: OSM way "Bokszutca" (Pit Lane), entry between Turn 13 and Turn 14, exit after Turn 1.
sources.trim: High-downforce, Monaco-like twisty circuit with one straight.
sources.pitLimit: F1 80 km/h (FIA Event Notes, Hungarian GP); TCR Europe 60 km/h (2026 TCR Europe Sporting Regulations art. 94, https://europe.tcr-series.com/pdf/2026_TCR_Europe_Sporting_Regs_V3_final.pdf; TCR Europe round 4, 3-5 Jul 2026). TCR pit loss omitted (no mandatory stops).
sources.pitLoss: Computed from Jolpica/Ergast lap times (in-lap + out-lap - 2 x median clean lap): median 21.0 s (2025), ~21.6 s (2026, clean stops); includes ~2.5 s stationary.
sources.raceLaps: 2026 Hungarian GP (round 11, 26 Jul 2026): 70 laps; not a sprint weekend.

notes: Turn numbering follows the F1 map (14 turns). Elevation from a 30 m surface model: broad shape only (~35 m range across the valley); fine detail and camber not resolved.
